thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Eval-gate alert fired: SAFETY_REGRESSION detected for model redwood-chat-13b-canary on promptset billing-templates. Gate score delta = -0.28, threshold -0.15. Paging on-call.

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-48291 created and paged to rotation 'eng-oncall' (urgent). Escalation policy: primary -> sec -> eng-sre.

oncall-rotation: paging aj (primary). Please acknowledge on PD.

aj: acked PD-48291. Taking this. Quick context?

incident-bot: Full eval summary: 15m window, 23 flagged responses (safety), 3 with high-severity PII/leak signals, model variant: redwood-chat-13b-canary@v2026-03-14-rc3, compared baseline redwood-chat-13b@v2026-03-13. Autocount: traffic routed 5% canary.

aj: thanks. @devon @sasha I need help confirming impact and a mitigation plan. If canary only has 5% traffic, likely limited customer exposure but those flagged responses may have slipped to a few users.

devon: on it. pulling sample logs and request ids now.

sasha: i'm rolling up the eval artifacts to check failure modes. initial glance shows prompt truncation + new decoding tweak in rc3 might be loosening safety constraints.

maria: cs-bot already sent a hold message to CS with the short blurb: "We detected potential unsafe outputs from a canary model; we are investigating. No broad outage. We'll update with findings."

aj: mitigation options: 1) Pause canary traffic (route 5% -> baseline) 2) Rollback canary to previous stable canary build 3) Disable the new decoding flag via config patch 4) Block specific promptset via safety proxy. I prefer immediate pause + rerun eval subset. Thoughts?

devon: pause canary now. Command: ```sh
# pause canary traffic
redwoodctl rollout pause --deployment redwood-chat-13b-canary
kubectl scale deployment/redwood-chat-13b-canary --replicas=0 -n inference-canary
``` Doing that in 10s.

aj: approved. devon, do the pause and then switch 100% of canary route to baseline. Command for routing: ```json
{
  "route": "redwood-chat-13b",
  "variant": "baseline",
  "weight": 100
}
# via API
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REX' https://controlplane/api/v1/routes/update -d @route.json
```

devon: canary paused. routing change pushed, waiting for propagation. Confirming token-level logs show traffic now flowing to baseline.

incident-bot: Routing change succeeded, propagation ack at 1768401263. Canary instances scaled to 0.

aj: good. next: run targeted safety eval on the baseline + rc3 artifact to ensure root cause. sasha, can you run focused eval on the 23 flagged inputs and a 200-sample neighborhood?

sasha: starting eval job: ```yaml
job: safety-retest
inputs: billing-templates-flagged
models: [redwood-chat-13b@v2026-03-13, redwood-chat-13b-canary@v2026-03-14-rc3]
timeout: 20m
``` ETA ~8-12m.

maria: CS asked if any paying customers saw bad outputs. devon: how many unique customer IDs in the 23 flags?

devon: 7 unique customer_ids, ~12 API keys. Two enterprise customers (cust-ALPHA, cust-BETA) had 3 and 2 flagged responses respectively. I'll open a targeted CS incident and flag for proactive outreach.

cs-bot: CS ticket CS-9214 created and assigned to Maria. Template message attached.

aj: action list so far:
- Pause canary & route traffic to baseline (done)
- Run focused eval vs baseline (in progress)
- Triage flagged responses + assemble examples for CS (devon)
- Decide on rollback or config revert based on eval (aj/sasha)
- If rollback, prepare canary artifact revert and release notes (devon)

sasha: initial eval results: rc3 shows consistent relaxation in the redaction heuristic; baseline passes the 23 flagged inputs (no high-sev). rc3 reproduces PII exposures in 3 samples. Looks like the new decode_tolerance parameter increased likelihood of hallucinated bank details.

aj: thanks. decision: we will not promote rc3. Two options: revert decode_tolerance config to previous value and re-run, or roll rc3 back entirely. Given speed, revert config on canary config store and keep canary paused until we validate.

devon: config patch ready. Patch command: ```sh
redwoodctl config set redwood-chat-13b-canary decode_tolerance 0.12 --env canary
redwoodctl config apply --env canary
``` Applying now.

incident-bot: Config apply succeeded at 1768401285.

sasha: rerunning the focused eval on rc3 with decode_tolerance=0.12 now. ETA 6m.

maria: CS update: "We've paused a canary model due to a safety regression that affected a small number of requests. We're proactively contacting impacted customers. No broad outage."

aj: good. metrics: number of flagged responses stopped increasing after routing change at 1768401263 which suggests mitigation worked. We'll still treat this as a safety incident.

sasha: rerun results: with decode_tolerance=0.12, rc3 no longer triggers the high-sev exposures on the 23 inputs. Pass.

aj: final plan: 1) keep canary paused and do another 1h full canary-eval sweep before any further rollout 2) mark rc3 as DO NOT PROMOTE until a proper fix & signoff 3) CS outreach to the 7 affected customers (Maria) 4) create postmortem and assign to eng-ml + eng-sre.

devon: creating artifact: INC-48291-mitigation-package, includes logs, eval runs, commands, and affected request ids. Dropping into S3 at s3://redwood-incidents/INC-48291.tar.gz

cs-bot: Notifying cust-ALPHA and cust-BETA via email template; flagged for immediate follow-up.

aj: closing PD incident once we confirm no new flags in 30m. For now: set status page note to "investigating - safety regression (canary paused)".

incident-bot: PD-48291 status changed to "acknowledged" -> awaiting resolution.

aj: thanks everyone. I'll hand this to eng-sre for follow-up and postmortem. @devon @sasha please sync on root cause writeup. I'll update the incident channel in 30m with closure or updates.

devon: cc'ing eng-sre on the artifact and monitoring rules to prevent similar decode_tolerance regressions from slipping through.

sasha: quick note for postmortem: add evaluation gate test for decode_tolerance parameter sensitivity and add an explicit PII redaction unit test.

aj: last check at 1768401299: no new flags in 30m window. I'm closing the active pager and marking incident as mitigated. We'll open a follow-up ticket for rollout gating improvements.

pagerduty: PD-48291 resolved by aj at 1768401299.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated. Follow-up owners: eng-ml (sasha), eng-sre (devon), product-safety (aj). Postmortem due in 3 business days.
